category_title: Students exhibiting aggressive behaviors and elopement during non-preferred academic tasks
minimal_context: Ann is assigned a counting worksheet at her desk while the tutor sits at least 6 feet away across the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Ann, it is time to do your counting worksheet. Please get started on the first problem.

STUDENT: (Stares at the paper without moving for over 5 seconds) Come over here right now! You have to sit next to me!

TUTOR: I am going to sit over here at my desk right now. You can do the worksheet by yourself.

STUDENT: (Stands up, leaving contact with her designated chair) No! I'm not doing it!

TUTOR: Ann, please sit back down and finish your counting.

STUDENT: (Yells loudly, throws her pencil across the room, and runs out of the classroom door) I'm leaving!

options.A: Start giving the student advanced, sixth-grade level counting worksheets to complete independently during the rest of the session.
options.B: Approach the situation from an affective lens, sharing personal experiences of being gifted and asking if she is satisfied with not utilizing her gifts.
options.C: Sit next to the student throughout the session and praise her for on-task behavior at least three times per minute.
options.D: Ask the student to identify the number on the worksheet, prompting her by stating that she already knows it.
